summaryBullets: Bottom of the Hill is leaking revenue first through no clear booking cta.
The audit used live public site data from https://bottomofthehill.com/.
There is no strong public signal for upcoming events, which likely hurts both discovery and fill rate.

leaks.title: No clear booking CTA
leaks.whyItMatters: Buyers cannot immediately see how to book the room, which increases drop-off from high-intent traffic.
leaks.fix: Add a primary 'Request a date' CTA on the homepage and every private events page.
leaks.evidence: No obvious 'book', 'rent', or private events CTA was detected.

leaks.title: High inquiry friction
leaks.whyItMatters: If prospects only see sparse contact information, fewer of them complete a booking inquiry.
leaks.fix: Publish a short venue inquiry form with event type, preferred dates, and expected attendance.
leaks.evidence: No inquiry form, phone number, or public booking email was found.

leaks.title: Missing rental and spec details
leaks.whyItMatters: Planners need capacity, room specs, and event-fit details before they reach out.
leaks.fix: Add a concise private events section with capacity, amenities, and AV/spec highlights.
leaks.evidence: Terms like capacity, rental, private event, or specs were not detected.

leaks.title: No promoter or artist intake path
leaks.whyItMatters: Without a submission flow, the venue misses inbound opportunities to fill weak nights.
leaks.fix: Add a lightweight artist/promoter intake form with draw, genre, and date range.
leaks.evidence: No artist submission or promoter intake terms were detected.

leaks.title: Missing or weak SEO metadata
leaks.whyItMatters: Search results underperform when the page title or description is generic or absent.
leaks.fix: Ship tighter title/meta tags focused on bookings, events, and the venue's city.
leaks.evidence: Title present: true. Meta description present: false.

leaks.title: Ticketing or upsell path is unclear
leaks.whyItMatters: Fans convert worse when ticket links are inconsistent and upsell messaging is absent.
leaks.fix: Standardize ticket links and add pre-event upsell blocks for VIP, merch, or drink packages.
leaks.evidence: No obvious ticketing provider or ticket CTA was detected.

leaks.title: No event schema markup detected
leaks.whyItMatters: Structured event data improves search visibility and helps search engines understand upcoming shows.
leaks.fix: Publish JSON-LD Event markup for upcoming shows or a reusable schema template.
leaks.evidence: No JSON-LD Event schema was detected in the page source.

leaks.title: No clear email capture
leaks.whyItMatters: Without email capture, the venue loses repeat demand from fans, promoters, and private-event prospects.
leaks.fix: Add a simple newsletter/signup block with one compelling incentive.
leaks.evidence: No newsletter or subscribe language was detected.

assumptions: Ranges assume the venue currently gets meaningful direct traffic but lacks one or more conversion-critical paths.
Inquiry uplift increases when a visible booking CTA and a low-friction form replace phone-only or buried contact flows.
Event uplift assumes promoter intake plus a visible upcoming-events surface help fill underbooked nights.

pricing.label: Performance-based
pricing.details: 12% of incremental booking revenue for the first 90 days, measured against a 60-day pre-launch baseline and tagged inquiry sources.

pricing.label: Flat setup + monthly
pricing.details: $1,500 setup + $350/mo for hosting, optimization, reporting, and monthly fix iterations.

fixAssets.description: Standalone booking page with a request-a-date CTA and inquiry form.
Promoter and artist intake form for filling open nights.
JSON-LD event schema or a reusable template.
Suggested title, meta description, H1, and OpenGraph tags.
Stub list of local promoter and artist targets inferred from genre signals.
